about: Interview for /workflow:plan-project. `wf plan questions` returns the next <= 4 unanswered questions (in this order) as AskUserQuestion payloads; answers are stored with `wf plan set KEY VALUE`. `detect` names a wf detect fact that answers the question without asking. `default` is what --defaults or a headless run records as an assumption. Free-text keys (product.summary, product.jobs) come from the idea argument or one plain chat question, never from AskUserQuestion.

text.prompt: One sentence: what it is and who it is for.
The three core jobs a user comes to do, as verbs ("book a room", "approve an invoice").

questions.question: What kind of product is it?

options.label: B2B SaaS
options.description: Organisations sign up; admins and staff use it every day.

options.label: Consumer app
options.description: Individuals sign up themselves; first-run and mobile matter most.

options.label: Internal tool
options.description: One organisation, known users, speed of building beats polish.

options.label: API or platform
options.description: Developers integrate with it; the contract is the product.

questions.question: Where will people use it? Pick every surface v1 must ship.

options.label: Web (desktop first)
options.description: Dense screens, keyboard, tables; still usable on a phone.

options.label: Web (phone first)
options.description: Most sessions on a phone browser; installable PWA possible.

options.label: Native mobile app
options.description: App store presence, device APIs, push.

options.label: API / CLI / device
options.description: A public API, a CLI, devices or a kiosk with no regular web UI.

questions.question: What does it store? Pick every one that applies.

options.label: Personal data (PII)
options.description: Names, emails, phone numbers, IDs, anything GDPR covers.

options.label: Money or payments
options.description: Prices, invoices, subscriptions, balances, payouts.

options.label: Many customer orgs
options.description: Multi-tenant: one org must never see another's data.

options.label: None of these
options.description: Public or non-sensitive data only.

questions.question: Expected size one year after launch?

options.label: Under 1k users
options.description: One small server is plenty.

options.label: 1k to 50k users
options.description: One server plus a managed database.

options.label: 50k to 1M users
options.description: Horizontal app servers, queues, caching.

options.label: Over 1M users
options.description: Performance and cost per request drive the stack.

questions.question: Which languages does whoever reviews the code (you or the team) read well?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Node, Bun, browser frameworks.

options.label: PHP
options.description: Laravel or Symfony.

options.label: Python
options.description: Django, FastAPI.

options.label: Go or Rust
options.description: Compiled services.

options.label: One VPS (Docker)
options.description: Cheapest and fully owned: docker compose or Kamal on a VPS.

options.label: Managed PaaS
options.description: Fly, Render, Railway, Laravel Cloud, Heroku-style deploys.

options.label: Serverless or edge
options.description: Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, Lambda.

options.label: Kubernetes / big cloud
options.description: AWS, GCP or Azure with an ops team.

questions.question: Monthly infrastructure budget for the first year?

options.label: Under $25
options.description: One small box, everything on it.

options.label: $25 to $150
options.description: App server plus managed database and backups.

options.label: $150 to $1000
options.description: Separate workers, staging, monitoring.

options.label: Over $1000
options.description: Cost is not the constraint.

questions.question: When must a first version be in real users' hands?

options.label: Within 4 weeks
options.description: Batteries-included stack, smallest possible v1.

options.label: Within 3 months
options.description: Room for the core plus quality gates from day one.

options.label: Within 6 months
options.description: Room for a design system and integrations.

options.label: No fixed date
options.description: Quality and long-term fit first.

questions.question: Which of these does v1 need? Pick every one that applies.

options.label: Works offline
options.description: Must keep working without a connection and sync later.

options.label: Live updates
options.description: Screens update by themselves (websockets, SSE).

options.label: Background jobs
options.description: Queues, schedules, imports, exports, emails.

options.label: None of these
options.description: Plain request and response.

questions.question: Which interface languages does v1 ship? Use Other to type locale codes, e.g. en, de, fi.

options.label: English only
options.description: Still i18n keys from day one, so adding a language is data, not a rewrite.

options.label: English + German
options.description: German is the width test for most European layouts.

options.label: English + Spanish
options.description: Latin American and Spanish markets.

options.label: English + French
options.description: French, Canadian and African francophone markets.

questions.question: What must it talk to in v1? Pick every one that applies.

options.label: Payments provider
options.description: Stripe, Paddle, a local bank gateway.

options.label: Email or SMS
options.description: Transactional mail, notifications.

options.label: Hardware or devices
options.description: Controllers, printers, scanners, IoT: needs an edge agent and simulators.

options.label: SSO or identity
options.description: Google/Microsoft login, SAML, OIDC.

questions.question: What already exists that the project must reuse?

options.label: Brand or design
options.description: Logo, colours, a Figma file or a design system.

options.label: Existing code
options.description: A predecessor app or prototype to mine.

options.label: Data to migrate
options.description: Spreadsheets or a database that must come along.

options.label: Nothing yet
options.description: Clean start.

questions.question: How much do you want to review yourself?

options.label: Every change
options.description: Each task stops in owner-review before it lands.

options.label: High-risk only
options.description: Auth, money, tenancy, migrations, infra stop for you; the rest lands on green gates.

options.label: Outcomes only
options.description: You check milestones and the board; agents land everything that passes.

widthFactor.about: Rough string expansion against English, used to pick ux.widestLocale. Higher is wider.
